newsitem.title: USA: Judge mulls request for Unabomber handwriting samples.
newsitem.headline: Judge mulls request for Unabomber handwriting samples.

text.p: A federal magistrate Thursday said he was likely to require Unabomber suspect Theodore Kaczynski to produce new handwriting samples for the prosecution.
Law enforcement officials believe Kaczynski, 54, is the shadowy Unabomber who killed three people and injured 23 during an anti-technology bombing campaign between 1978 and 1995.
His Sacramento trial, expected to begin in November, will involve charges stemming from only four of the bombings and two of the killings. He has also been charged with a killing in New Jersey.
Kaczynski, who has pleaded not guilty, did not appear in court for Thursday's 45-minute hearing before U.S. Magistrate Judge Gregory Hollows in Sacramento.
At the hearing, the prosecution asked Hollows to order Kaczynski to produce handwriting samples in English and Spanish and in "numeric codes."

Prosecutor Bernard Hubley said the government needed handwriting samples of the "best standard" in order to authenticate Kaczynski's authorship of hundreds of letters and documents federal agents seized from his remote Montana cabin.
Defence attorneys urged Hollows to reject the government's request, arguing that the government already had more than 800 pages of Kaczynski's writing.
"They are asking us to create evidence," said Quin Denvir, Kaczynski's chief defence attorney. "It's not at all clear they have that right."
"How far does the defendant have to go to assist the government in preparing its case?" added defence attorney Judy Clarke.

Hollows said he would take the government's request under submission and did not say how long it would take to reach his decision. But Hollows said it was his "tentative ruling" to grant the government a limited number of new samples.

Hollows said he was inclined to limit the number of samples to 60 paragraphs, ranging from three to 15 lines or approximately 120 words, and may also have Kaczynski prepare a complete set of upper and lower case letters and numbers.
Hollows said he may also limit the amount of time Kaczynski would spend writing out the samples, probably to a one day session at the Sacramento jail where he is being held.
